svg.title: Hipparchus, two stations on the Earth and a shared solar direction
svg.desc: Hellespont and Alexandria lie on the Earth's circle, Hellespont north of Alexandria. From each station a line goes to the Moon, and a parallel line marks the Sun's direction. The Moon is much too close, so the angle is enlarged. Latitudes are only approximately 41 and 31 degrees.
svg.text: Two places on the Earth, one Moon, parallel sunlight
Stations are on the circle. Grey lines are parallel. The Moon is drawn much too close.
Both dots are on the circle. Hellespont is north of Alexandria. The grey lines are parallel. The Moon is drawn much too close, so the angle is enlarged.
Total at the Hellespont. At Alexandria four-fifths of the diameter was covered, so about one-fifth stayed bright.
